summary: Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, ENLOV, and EPHE (~1958–1962). He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1970) and Leiden University (~1993–1999).

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009) and later served there as a research fellow around 2009.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Calcutta, where she was attested in 1966, studying under Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Allahabad. He taught at Calcutta (~1919–1924) and Allahabad (~1924–1956), and served as Ex-Director at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1956–1968).

K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hong Kong.

Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke (1920–1970) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge, and later served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1923). He held posts at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1932–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1960), Komazawa University, and Japan Women's University.

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and under Franklin Edgerton. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1957–1963) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1963–1988).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1996).

Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Kiel (~1956–1961). He held positions at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1974) and served as a professor at Saarland University (attested 2010).

Kuntala Bhattacharya works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee, Shyamapada Misra, and Prabal Kumar Sen, and held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).

Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at UCLA by 1997 and served as an Assistant Curator in the Asian Art department at the Metropolitan Museum of Art around 2005.
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1913–1917). He later held an academic post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1920 until 1943.

Kurt Tropper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and Richard Salomon and at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp, later holding posts at Alabama and Virginia.
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1929–2012) was a Buddhist studies figure who served as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested in 1998 and 2009).

Kwangsoo Park is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He is attested as a professor at Wonkwang University in 2020.

Kyo Kano (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. He held an assistant post at Kyoto University (1989) and was an associate professor at Kobe Women's University (2000).

Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Taisho University. He later held a post at Taisho University and served as head priest (貫主) of Senso-ji from around 1952 to 1979.
